`chartLocus` directly: the openness of `chartLocus` is a separate obligation
(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the

def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)

/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    (V : D.left.Opens)
    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :
    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V h

/-! ## The structure morphism of a restricted chart -/

/-- **The structure morphism of a restricted chart is the restriction of the structure
morphism.**  Hence the `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` hypothesis of
`JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited by every restriction: being locally of finite type is
local on the source, and an open immersion is locally of finite type.


=== ChartFibrePresented ===
  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.

Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)

  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/

  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the

  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),

9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/

59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
60	
61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
67	
68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
72	
73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
75	cover. -/
76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))
81	
82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
87	  Iff.rfl

89	/-! ## Transport along refinement maps -/
90	
91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
94	  ext x
95	  simp [doubleInl]
96	
97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
100	  ext x
101	  simp [doubleInr]
102	
103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
125	
126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2
131	
132	@[simp]
133	lemma descentMap_coe {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
134	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
135	    (descentMap C h x : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
136	      = relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
137	  rfl
138	
139	@[simp]
140	lemma descentMap_id {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (x : descentClasses C E) :
141	    descentMap C (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier) x = x := by
142	  ext
143	  rw [descentMap_coe,
144	    show (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k = AlgHom.id k E.Carrier from rfl]
145	  exact relPicAlgMap_id C _
146	
147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
150	  ext
151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]
154	  exact relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
155	
156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
168	    ext y
169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
171	    ext y
172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
180	        rw [hx']
181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]
184	
185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
187	all choices. -/
188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)
192	
193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
194	
195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
201	  iseqv := by
202	    constructor
203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]

213	/-- The one-step étale plus of the relative Picard functor at the affine test `Spec A`:
214	relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
215	modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
216	sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
217	étale-separated — proved separately). -/
218	def PicEtAff : Type u :=
219	  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))

223	/-- The plus class of a relative Picard class with a descent condition on a cover. -/
224	def mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) : PicEtAff C A :=
225	  Quotient.mk _ ⟨E, x⟩

227	@[elab_as_elim]
228	theorem ind {motive : PicEtAff C A → Prop}
229	    (mk : ∀ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E), motive (mk C E x)) :
230	    ∀ q, motive q := by
231	  intro q
232	  induction q using Quotient.ind with
233	  | _ p => exact mk p.1 p.2

235	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
236	    {y : descentClasses C F} :
237	    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
238	      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
239	        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=
240	  Quotient.eq

242	/-- Transporting the representative to a finer cover does not change the plus class. -/
243	@[simp]
244	theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
245	    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
246	  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩

250	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
251	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
252	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
253	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
254	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
255	      = descentMap C f x := by
256	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]
257	
258	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the right factor. -/
259	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inr {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
260	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
261	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
262	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)
263	      = descentMap C g y := by
264	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInr]

266	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
267	-- The `rw` chain unifies `descentMap` nests whose `AlgHom` instance arguments run through
268	-- quotient and tensor-product carriers; the unifications are heartbeat-hungry.
269	private lemma mulLift_compat (p q p' q' : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E)
270	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') :
271	    mk C (p.1.prod q.1)
272	        (descentMap C (p.1.prodInl q.1) p.2 * descentMap C (p.1.prodInr q.1) q.2)
273	      = mk C (p'.1.prod q'.1)
274	        (descentMap C (p'.1.prodInl q'.1) p'.2
275	          * descentMap C (p'.1.prodInr q'.1) q'.2) := by
276	  obtain ⟨F, f, f', hf⟩ := hp
277	  obtain ⟨G, g, g', hg⟩ := hq
278	  refine (mk_eq_mk_iff C).mpr ⟨F.prod G,
279	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f) ((F.prodInr G).comp g),
280	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f') ((F.prodInr G).comp g'), ?_⟩
281	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, descentMap_prodLift_inl, descentMap_prodLift_inr,
282	    descentMap_prodLift_inl, descentMap_prodLift_inr, descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp,
283	    descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hf, hg]

285	instance : Mul (PicEtAff C A) :=
286	  ⟨fun a b => Quotient.liftOn₂ a b

288	      (descentMap C (p.1.prodInl q.1) p.2 * descentMap C (p.1.prodInr q.1) q.2))
289	    fun p q p' q' hp hq => mulLift_compat C p q p' q' hp hq⟩

291	lemma mk_mul_mk (E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E)
292	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
293	    mk C E x * mk C F y
294	      = mk C (E.prod F)
295	          (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x * descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y) :=
296	  rfl

298	/-- Multiplication of two classes represented on the *same* cover is represented by the
299	product on that cover — the descent condition makes the two transports to the common
300	refinement agree. -/
301	theorem mk_mul_mk_same (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x y : descentClasses C E) :
302	    mk C E x * mk C E y = mk C E (x * y) := by
303	  have h : descentMap C (E.prodInl E) x * descentMap C (E.prodInl E) y
304	      = descentMap C (E.prodInl E) (x * y) :=
305	    (map_mul _ x y).symm
306	  rw [mk_mul_mk, descentMap_congr C (E.prodInr E) (E.prodInl E) y, h, mk_descentMap]

309	  ⟨mk C (.self A) 1⟩

315	theorem mk_one (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) : mk C E 1 = 1 :=

338	  mul_assoc a b c := by
339	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
340	    induction b using ind with | _ F y =>

347	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
348	    rw [one_def, mk_mul_mk, map_one, one_mul, mk_descentMap]
349	  mul_one a := by
350	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
351	    rw [one_def, mk_mul_mk, map_one, mul_one, mk_descentMap]
352	  inv_mul_cancel a := by
353	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
354	    rw [mk_inv, mk_mul_mk_same, inv_mul_cancel, mk_one]

356	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
357	    induction b using ind with | _ F y =>
358	    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x, ← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y,

361	/-! ### The unit of the plus construction -/
362	
363	/-- Every class pulled back from the base carries the tautological descent datum: the two
364	composites `A → B ⇉ B ⊗[A] B` coincide. -/
365	lemma tautological_mem_descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
366	    (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
367	    relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) x
368	      ∈ descentClasses C E := by
369	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
370	  congr 2
371	  ext a
372	  simp [doubleInl, doubleInr, Algebra.ofId_apply]
373	
374	variable (A) in
375	/-- The unit of the plus construction: a relative Picard class of the affine test,
376	pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological descent datum. -/
377	def unit : relPic C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A where
378	  toFun x := mk C (.self A)
379	    ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
380	  map_one' := by
381	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) 1⟩ :
382	        descentClasses C (.self A)) = 1 from Subtype.ext (map_one _), mk_one]
383	  map_mul' x y := by
384	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) (x * y)⟩ :
385	        descentClasses C (.self A))
386	        = ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
387	          * ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) y⟩ from
388	      Subtype.ext (map_mul _ x y), ← mk_mul_mk_same]
389

10	
11	The Layer-2 étale Picard functor `picEt` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEt`,
12	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`) receives the honest relative Picard functor
13	through a natural transformation — the **unit of the étale sheafification**
14	(gap G4 of `informal/zeta-c2-rigidification-recon.md`, shared prerequisite of the
15	global (C2) comparison and of the degree/`Pic⁰` interface):
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T U`: the spectrum of the section ring of an
18	  affine open `U` of a test object `T`, as a test object over `T` — the bridge between
19	  the affine-opens indexing of `picEt` and the test-object indexing of `relPic`.  Its
20	  coherences: restriction (`fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom`) and naturality along an
21	  arbitrary test morphism (`fromSpecAffine_naturality`).
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEt C T`: the component at `T` — a relative Picard class
23	  restricts along `fromSpecAffine T U` to every affine open, and each restriction is
24	  sent into the plus construction by `PicEtAff.unit`; the family is compatible by
25	  `PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit` and the coherences.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`: **affine consistency** — on an
27	  affine test the component collapses through the affine comparison
28	  (`picEtAffineEquiv`) to the unit `PicEtAff.unit` of the plus construction, so the
29	  Layer-2 unit extends the affine unit.
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtUnit C : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`: the natural
31	  transformation (naturality through the `∃!`-API `picEt.IsPullbackValue` of
32	  `picEtMapVal`).
33	
34	The (C2) comparison (`PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`, recon §1.3) will upgrade
35	the affine components to isomorphisms over section-admitting tests; injectivity of the
36	affine components is the landed (C1) `PicEtAff.unit_injective`.
37	-/
38	
39	set_option autoImplicit false

41	universe u

45	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

47	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

49	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

51	noncomputable section

53	/-! ## The affine-open test objects of a test object -/
54	
55	namespace Over
56	
57	/-- The spectrum of the section ring of an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, as a test object
58	over `T`: the underlying morphism is `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec`, and it lies over `Spec k`
59	by the very definition of the section-ring algebra `Over.sectionsAlgebra`. -/
60	def fromSpecAffine (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
61	    overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1) ⟶ T :=
62	  Over.homMk U.2.fromSpec (by
63	    have h1 : Spec.map (T.hom.appLE ⊤ U.1
64	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge))
65	          ≫ (isAffineOpen_top (Spec (.of k))).fromSpec
66	        = U.2.fromSpec ≫ T.hom :=
67	      IsAffineOpen.SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec T.hom (isAffineOpen_top _) U.2 _
68	    have h2 : (isAffineOpen_top (Spec (.of k))).fromSpec
69	        = Spec.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv := by
70	      rw [IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_top, Scheme.isoSpec_Spec_inv]
71	    change U.2.fromSpec ≫ T.hom
72	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(T.left, U.1)))
73	    rw [Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Spec.map_comp, ← h2, h1])
74	
75	/-- **Naturality of `fromSpecAffine`** along an arbitrary morphism of test objects:
76	for affine opens `W ≤ f⁻¹ V`, the section-ring pullback `Over.appLEAlgHom` intertwines
77	the affine-open test objects — `IsAffineOpen.SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec` in the over
78	category. -/
79	theorem fromSpecAffine_naturality {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
80	    (V : T.left.affineOpens) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) (e : W.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) :
81	    Over.overSpecMap (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W.1 e) ≫ fromSpecAffine T V
82	      = fromSpecAffine T' W ≫ f := by
83	  ext : 1
84	  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W.1 e).toRingHom)
85	      ≫ V.2.fromSpec = W.2.fromSpec ≫ f.left
86	  have h : CommRingCat.ofHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W.1 e).toRingHom
87	      = f.left.appLE V.1 W.1 e := rfl
88	  rw [h]
89	  exact IsAffineOpen.SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec f.left V.2 W.2 e
90	
91	/-- **Restriction coherence of `fromSpecAffine`**: the affine-open test object of a
92	smaller affine open factors through that of a larger one, along `Spec` of the section
93	restriction. -/
94	theorem fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {U V : T.left.affineOpens}
95	    (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
96	    Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T h) ≫ fromSpecAffine T V = fromSpecAffine T U := by
97	  have he : U.1 ≤ (Over.Hom.left (𝟙 T)) ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 := fun x hx => by
98	    rw [Over.id_left]
99	    exact h hx
100	  rw [← Over.appLEAlgHom_id T V.1 U.1 he h, fromSpecAffine_naturality (𝟙 T) V U he,
101	    Category.comp_id]
102	
103	/-- On an affine test, the affine-open test object of the top affine open is the test
104	itself: composing with the `ΓSpecIso` identification of the section ring with the test
105	algebra gives the identity. -/
106	theorem overSpecMap_ΓTop_fromSpecAffine_top (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
107	    Over.overSpecMap (k := k) (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
108	        ≫ fromSpecAffine (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A) = 𝟙 (overSpec k A) := by
109	  have key : Spec.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).hom
110	      ≫ (isAffineOpen_top (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))).fromSpec
111	      = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := by
112	    rw [IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_top, Scheme.isoSpec_Spec_inv, ← Spec.map_comp,
113	      Iso.inv_hom_id, Spec.map_id]
114	  ext : 1
115	  exact key
116	
117	end Over
118	
119	/-! ## The component at a test object -/
120	
121	/-- The component at a test object `T` of the unit of the étale sheafification: a
122	relative Picard class restricts along `Over.fromSpecAffine T U` to every affine open
123	`U ⊆ T.left`, and each restriction enters the plus construction through
124	`PicEtAff.unit`.  The family is compatible under restriction by naturality of the unit
125	(`PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit`) and the restriction coherence of `fromSpecAffine`. -/
126	def relPicToPicEt (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : relPic C T →* picEt C T where
127	  toFun z :=
128	    ⟨fun U => PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T.left, U.1) (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) z),
129	      fun U V h => by
130	        rw [PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit]
131	        refine congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T.left, U.1)) ?_
132	        calc relPicAlgMap C (Over.resAlgHom T h)
133	              (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T V) z)
134	            = relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T h)
135	                ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine T V) z :=
136	              (relPicMap_comp C (Over.fromSpecAffine T V)
137	                (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T h)) z).symm
138	          _ = relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) z := by
139	              rw [Over.fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom h]⟩
140	  map_one' := by
141	    refine picEt.ext fun U => ?_
142	    change PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T.left, U.1) (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) 1) = 1
143	    rw [map_one, map_one]
144	  map_mul' z w := by
145	    refine picEt.ext fun U => ?_
146	    change PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T.left, U.1) (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) (z * w))
147	      = PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T.left, U.1) (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) z)
148	        * PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T.left, U.1) (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) w)
149	    rw [map_mul, map_mul]
150	
151	@[simp]
152	lemma relPicToPicEt_val (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (z : relPic C T)
153	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
154	    (relPicToPicEt C T z).1 U
155	      = PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T.left, U.1) (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) z) :=
156	  rfl
157	
158	/-- **Affine consistency of the unit**: on an affine test `overSpec k A` the component
159	`relPicToPicEt` collapses, through the affine comparison `picEtAffineEquiv`, to the
160	unit `PicEtAff.unit` of the plus construction. -/
161	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
162	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
163	    picEtAffineEquiv C A (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z) = PicEtAff.unit C A z :=
164	  calc picEtAffineEquiv C A (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z)
165	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
166	          (PicEtAff.unit C Γ((overSpec k A).left, (overSpecTopAffine A).1)
167	            (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A))
168	              z)) := rfl
169	    _ = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicAlgMap C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
170	          (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A)) z)) :=
171	        PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit C _ _
172	    _ = PicEtAff.unit C A
173	          (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap (k := k) (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
174	            ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A)) z) :=
175	        congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C A)
176	          (relPicMap_comp C (Over.fromSpecAffine (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A))
177	            (Over.overSpecMap (k := k) (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom) z).symm
178	    _ = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMap C (𝟙 (overSpec k A)) z) :=
179	        congrArg (fun g : overSpec k A ⟶ overSpec k A =>
180	            PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMap C g z))
181	          (Over.overSpecMap_ΓTop_fromSpecAffine_top A)
182	    _ = PicEtAff.unit C A z := congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C A) (relPicMap_id C z)
183	
184	/-! ## The natural transformation -/
185	
186	section unit
187	
188	variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
189	
190	/-- Naturality of the components: restriction of the unit's image along an arbitrary
191	morphism of test objects is the unit's image of the restricted class.  Verified through
192	the `∃!`-characterization `picEt.IsPullbackValue` of the glued value of `picEtMap`,
193	using both coherences of `fromSpecAffine`. -/
194	theorem picEtMap_relPicToPicEt {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
195	    (z : relPic C T) :
196	    picEtMap C f (relPicToPicEt C T z) = relPicToPicEt C T' (relPicMap C f z) := by
197	  refine picEt.ext fun W => ?_
198	  rw [picEtMap_val]
199	  refine picEtMapVal_eq_of C f (relPicToPicEt C T z) ?_
200	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
201	  rw [relPicToPicEt_val, relPicToPicEt_val, PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit, PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit]
202	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C Γ(T'.left, W₀.1)) ?_
203	  calc relPicAlgMap C (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀)
204	        (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T' W) (relPicMap C f z))
205	      = relPicAlgMap C (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀)
206	          (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T' W ≫ f) z) := by
207	        rw [relPicMap_comp C f (Over.fromSpecAffine T' W) z]
208	    _ = relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀)
209	          ≫ (Over.fromSpecAffine T' W ≫ f)) z :=
210	        (relPicMap_comp C (Over.fromSpecAffine T' W ≫ f)
211	          (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀)) z).symm
212	    _ = relPicMap C ((Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀)
213	          ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine T' W) ≫ f) z := by
214	        rw [Category.assoc]
215	    _ = relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T' W₀ ≫ f) z := by
216	        rw [Over.fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom hW₀]
217	    _ = relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV)
218	          ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine T V) z := by
219	        rw [Over.fromSpecAffine_naturality f V W₀ hV]
220	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV)
221	          (relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T V) z) :=
222	        relPicMap_comp C (Over.fromSpecAffine T V)
223	          (Over.overSpecMap (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV)) z
224	
225	/-- **The unit of the étale sheafification** (gap G4 of the (C2) recon): the natural
226	transformation from the honest relative Picard functor into the étale-sheafified
227	Layer-2 functor.  On affine tests it is the unit of the plus construction
228	(`picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`); its affine components are injective by the (C1)
229	étale separatedness (`PicEtAff.unit_injective`), and bijective over section-admitting
230	tests by the (C2) comparison. -/
231	def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
232	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicToPicEt C T.unop)
233	  naturality T T' g := by
234	    ext z
235	    exact (picEtMap_relPicToPicEt C g.unop z).symm
236	
237	@[simp]
238	lemma picEtUnit_app (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (z : relPic C T.unop) :
239	    (picEtUnit C).app T z = relPicToPicEt C T.unop z :=
240	  rfl
241	
242	/-- Affine consistency of the unit, natural-transformation form. -/
243	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_picEtUnit_app (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
244	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
245	    picEtAffineEquiv C A ((picEtUnit C).app (op (overSpec k A)) z)
246	      = PicEtAff.unit C A z :=
247	  picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A z
248	
249	end unit

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityMoving

/-!
# The (C2) effectivity theorem and the surjectivity close

**The campaign close.**  The fppf-effectivity theorem of the (C2) campaign (Kleiman,
*The Picard Scheme*, `th:cmp` Part 2 recast on the cocycle model) and the resulting
bijectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction over section-admitting field
tests:

* `Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces` — effectivity for an arbitrary
  faithfully flat `A → B`, given a covering family of trivialized pieces: a rigidified
  class on the cover curve whose two coprojection pullbacks agree on the nose descends
  along the cover inclusion `cg`.  The σ-normalized comparison exists unconditionally
  (E1); flat trivializations come from the trivialized pieces by localize-and-flatten;
  the refinement splice assembles the descent.
* `Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq` — **the (C2) effectivity theorem** for a
  module-finite faithfully flat cover: the covering family of trivialized pieces is
  produced *unconditionally* by the moving lemma
  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityMoving`).  Module-finiteness is honest: for a
  merely quasi-finite étale cover the bare restricted class need not trivialize on any
  saturated piece (see the moving lemma's docstring); the close below reaches arbitrary
  étale covers of a field test through the field cofinality of étale covers.
* `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` — **the headline**: over a field test `K`
  admitting a curve point `σ : Spec K ⟶ C`, the unit of the étale plus construction is
  surjective.  A plus class is represented on a finite separable field-extension cover
  (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`); the rigidification layer
  (G1 + the rigidified transport keystone) puts the representative in the effectivity
  theorem's hypotheses; the descended class maps to the original by `mk`-calculus.
* `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` — with the (C1) injectivity (étale separatedness),
  the unit is a group isomorphism `relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
  TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

section effectivity

variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B]

/-- **The (C2) effectivity theorem** (recon §0.3; Kleiman `th:cmp` Part 2, the descent
of the rigidified pair): for a module-finite faithfully flat cover `A → B` of the test
algebra of a curve point `σ`, every Čech Picard class on the cover curve `X_B` that is
rigidified along the base-changed section (`hrig`) and has equal coprojection pullbacks
on the curve over `B ⊗[A] B` (`hdesc`) descends along the cover inclusion:
`∃ M, cg^* M = L`. -/
theorem exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq [Module.Finite A B]
    (L : (XB).CechPic)
    (hrig : Over.IsRigidified
      (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ) L)
    (hdesc : Scheme.CechPic.map (u₁) L = Scheme.CechPic.map (u₂) L) :
    ∃ M : (XA).CechPic, Scheme.CechPic.map (cg) M = L := by
  induction L using Scheme.CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒩 a

  rw [show (Quot.mk _ γ : (XB).unitsH1 𝒩)

/-! ## The surjectivity close (recon §0.2) -/

section close

variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- **Surjectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction over a section-admitting
field test** (Kleiman 2.5(2), axiom (C2) — the campaign headline): if the curve admits
a `K`-point `σ`, every class of `PicEtAff C K` comes from a relative Picard class.

A representative on an étale cover of `Spec K` is refined to a finite separable field
extension (field cofinality); the rigidification layer produces a rigidified Čech
representative whose descent equation holds on the nose; the (C2) effectivity theorem
descends it along the cover inclusion; and the `relPicMk`/`mk`-calculus identifies the
descended class's unit with the original plus class. -/
theorem PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    Function.Surjective (PicEtAff.unit C K) := by
  intro q
  induction q using PicEtAff.ind with | _ E x
  classical
  -- ### refine the representing cover to a finite separable field extension
  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hLalg, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨f⟩⟩ :=
    E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
  set F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L with hF
  set g : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] F.Carrier :=
    ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom).comp f with hg
  set y : descentClasses C F := descentMap C g x with hy
  have hq : PicEtAff.mk C E x = PicEtAff.mk C F y :=
    (PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C g x).symm
  haveI : Module.Finite K F.Carrier :=
    Module.Finite.equiv (R := K) (M := L)
      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toLinearEquiv
  -- ### a rigidified representative of the descent class (G1)
  obtain ⟨Lc, hrig, hLcrep⟩ := relPic.exists_isRigidified_rep
    (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ)
    (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
  have hmem : relPicMk C (overSpec k F.Carrier) Lc ∈ descentClasses C F := by
    rw [hLcrep]
    exact y.2
  -- ### the on-the-nose descent equation (the rigidified transport keystone)
  have hdesc0 := Over.IsRigidified.cechPicMap_doubleInl_eq_doubleInr σ hmem hrig
  have hinl : doubleInl (k := k) F = tensorInl (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
  have hinr : doubleInr (k := k) F = tensorInr (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
  rw [hinl, hinr] at hdesc0
  -- ### the effectivity theorem
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq C σ Lc hrig hdesc0
  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M, ?_⟩
  -- ### the `mk`-calculus close
  rw [PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C F (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M)]
  rw [hq]
  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C F) (Subtype.ext ?_)
  change relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
      (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M) = (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
  rw [relPicAlgMap, relPicMap_mk, hM, hLcrep]

/-- **The unit of the étale plus construction is an isomorphism over a
section-admitting field test** — étale separatedness (C1) plus effectivity (C2):
`relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`. -/
noncomputable def PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    relPic C (overSpec k K) ≃* PicEtAff C K :=
  MulEquiv.ofBijective (PicEtAff.unit C K)
    ⟨PicEtAff.unit_injective C K, PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section C K σ⟩

end close

/-- A presented étale cover of `Spec A`: a finite-variable polynomial presentation of an
étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum maps onto `Spec A`.  Presentations keep the type of covers
small (`Type u` for `A : Type u`), which is what makes the étale plus construction over
these covers a legitimate colimit; the carrier-level content is recovered by
`Algebra.EtaleCover.of`/`ofEquiv`. -/
structure EtaleCover (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Type u where
  /-- The number of variables of the presentation. -/
  n : ℕ
  /-- The ideal of relations of the presentation. -/
  ideal : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
  /-- The presented algebra is étale over the base. -/
  etale : Algebra.Etale A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)
  /-- The spectrum of the presented algebra covers the spectrum of the base. -/
  comap_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)))

namespace EtaleCover

variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]

/-- The covering algebra presented by an étale cover. -/
protected abbrev Carrier (E : EtaleCover A) : Type u :=
  MvPolynomial (Fin E.n) A ⧸ E.ideal

instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier :=
  E.etale

instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier :=
  .of_comap_surjective E.comap_surjective

theorem prod_refines_left (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E :=

theorem prod_refines_right (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E' :=

theorem exists_refines_prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
    ∃ E'' : EtaleCover A, E''.Refines E ∧ E''.Refines E' :=
  ⟨E.prod E', E.prod_refines_left E', E.prod_refines_right E'⟩

/-- The trivial cover of `Spec A` by itself. -/
noncomputable def self (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : EtaleCover A :=
  .of A (by
    rw [show algebraMap A A = RingHom.id A from rfl, PrimeSpectrum.comap_id]
    exact fun p => ⟨p, rfl⟩)

/-- The carrier of the trivial cover is the base ring. -/
noncomputable def selfEquiv (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : (self A).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] A :=
  ofEquiv A _

structure map of the carrier, through the trivial carrier's identification with `A`). -/
noncomputable def fromSelf (E : EtaleCover A) : (self A).Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier :=
  (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).comp (selfEquiv A).toAlgHom

/-- Every cover refines the trivial cover: the trivial cover is the base point of the
refinement preorder. -/
theorem refines_self (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines (self A) :=
  ⟨E.fromSelf⟩

/-- Naturality of the Σ-family: it pulls back to itself under every test map. -/
theorem sigmaFamily_natural (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

    picEtMap C f (sigmaFamily C Z T) = sigmaFamily C Z T' :=
  thetaFamily_natural C _ f

/-- **The degree of the Σ-family at every field point is `deg k Z`** (E-iv-alg under
the DAT-5 degree law + E-i). -/
theorem degAt_sigmaFamily (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :

  change degAt (thetaFamily C (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass k Z) T) t = _
  rw [degAt_thetaFamily, classDeg_picClass]

`m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family,

    * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m)⁻¹

/-!
# A plus class becomes honest over its own étale carrier — over an ARBITRARY affine base

This closes the obligation the CHART-U(b) header table names "honesty over a general affine
base" (issue I-0558), and it needs no field.

## The obligation, and why it looked hard

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean`'s route needs a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over an affine base
whose class is the (collapsed) twisted class.  `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) supplies the datum — but it takes an **honest Čech
class** `c` over the base as a *hypothesis*, and a plus class over `Spec A` is not honest: it is
`PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E` of `A`.

The tree's only route from a plus class to an honest one was
`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s `exists_splitting_of_picEt`, which requires `[Field K]` — its
engine is étale field-cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`),
false over a general base.  So the obligation read as: find a *substitute* for cofinality over
`Spec A`.

## Why it is in fact free

There is no substitute needed, because **a cover splits over its own carrier**.  The
field-cofinality theorem is used to produce an `A`-algebra map `E.Carrier →ₐ L` into something
where the class becomes a unit; but the identity `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier` is already such a
map, and it exists for every cover over every base.  Restricting the plus class along
`A → E.Carrier` therefore makes it honest, with no finiteness, separability, or field
hypothesis anywhere.

Concretely `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x` — the
transported class is presented by `x` itself.  The proof is the general-base analogue of
`PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`), which is stated
only for fields; the field hypotheses there are inherited from *its* consumer (the degree seam,
which reads a degree and so needs a field), not required by the argument.  The one substantive
step is the same in both: the descent condition `x.2`, fed to `relPicAlgMap_congr`, identifies
the two ways of transporting `x` to the base-changed carrier.

## What this does and does not give

It gives honesty **over `Spec E.Carrier`**, not over `Spec A`.  That is exactly what the
(b-amendment) asks for — its step is "over the étale carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is
honest", after which the engine fires on `Spec B` and transport (ii) pushes the open locus down
to `Spec A` along the (open, surjective) carrier map.  Nothing here performs that descent; the
topological core of it is landed as `isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:129`).

So after this file the CHART-U(b) route has ONE remaining obligation, the pointwise
`IsChartDatumPresentation` — and, unlike the previous "one remaining obligation" claims on this
lane, that one is a genuine statement about matching two fibre predicates, not a missing
construction.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` — **a plus class is honest over its own
  cover carrier**, over an arbitrary affine base.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_honest_of_picEtAff` — the existential form.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist` — the payoff, in the engine's shape: over
  a base where the class is honest, a datum presenting it twisted by any chart index exists.
-/

variable (C) in
/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.

The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
it, and every point `t` of `T`:

* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.

Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.

**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.

The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)

/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening

A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**

The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.

**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩

end

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## Honesty over the cover's own carrier -/

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- **A plus class becomes the plus-unit of an honest class over its own cover carrier**, over
an ARBITRARY affine base `A` — no field, no finiteness, no separability.

`PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x`: the class
presented by `x` on the cover `E` restricts, along `A → E.Carrier`, to the tautological plus
unit of `x` itself.

This is the general-base analogue of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom`
(`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`) at `ℓ := AlgHom.id`.  That lemma carries `[Field K]`,
`[Field L]` because *its* consumer (the degree seam) reads a degree; the argument itself uses
neither.  The substantive content, identical in both, is the **descent condition** `x.2`: the
two ways of carrying `x` into the base-changed carrier — along `E.baseChangeInclude` and along
`Algebra.ofId` — agree on a descent class, which is what `relPicAlgMap_congr` consumes.

Why this matters: the tree's only previous route from a plus class to an honest one was étale
field-cofinality (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`), which is field-only, so "honesty over a general
affine base" was recorded as an unlanded *construction*.  It is not a construction at all — a
cover splits over its own carrier, and the identity map is the splitting. -/
theorem PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
    PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
      = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
  rw [PicEtAff.map_mk, PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)]
  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)) (Subtype.ext ?_)
  rw [descentBaseChange_coe]
  exact relPicAlgMap_congr C (E.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier)
    ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier (E.baseChange E.Carrier).Carrier).restrictScalars A) x.2

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- **Every plus class over an affine base is honest over some affine base above it** — the
existential form of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self`, which is how a consumer meets it: it does
not get to choose `B`, it gets a `B` from the class's own presentation.

Compare `exists_splitting_of_picEt` (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`): that gives a *field*
extension and requires the base to be a field; this gives an étale extension and requires
nothing.  The two are the field and general-base halves of the same move, and the chart layer
needs both — the field one to read the split witness predicate at a point, this one to run the
engine over a base. -/
theorem exists_honest_of_picEtAff {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (a : PicEtAff C A) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra k B) (_ : Algebra A B)
        (_ : IsScalarTower k A B) (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)),
      PicEtAff.map C B a = PicEtAff.unit C B z := by
  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
  | mk E x =>
    refine ⟨E.Carrier, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)), ?_⟩
    exact PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self C E x

/-! ## The payoff: the engine's input, with honesty discharged -/

variable (C π) in
/-- **The engine input, assembled**: for any plus class over any affine base `A` and any chart
index `(m, Z)`, once the class is read honestly over a base `B` above `A` by a Čech class `c`,
a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `B` presenting `c` twisted by the chart index exists.

This composes the two halves that were previously recorded as separate gates:

* honesty over `B := E.Carrier` — `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` above, which needs no field;
* presentation of the twisted class by a datum — `exists_cechPicClass_eq`, applied at the
  *product* class, which is why no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul` is needed
  (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`).

The conclusion is exactly the input of
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`, so the openness of the witness
locus over `Spec B` is available for every plus class and every chart index.  What is *not* here
is the identification of that locus with `chartLocus` — that is `IsChartDatumPresentation`, the
one genuine remaining obligation of CHART-U(b).

Stated with `c` as a hypothesis rather than bundled into the existential: bundling it forces the
elaborator to unify the tower instances on `B` while `B` is still a metavariable, which is the
hazard recorded at `Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s closing note.  A consumer obtains `B` and `c`
from `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` plus `relPicMk_surjective`, then applies this. -/
theorem exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (m : ℕ)
    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
      D.cechPicClass
        = c * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k B) (chartTwistClass C m Z) :=
  exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass c m Z

end

end AlgebraicGeometry
